1.subject: chore: establish project configuration
body: Establish repository ignore rules, pytest bootstrap configuration, and the initial Kaggle package boundary.
Make the project importable from tests without introducing runtime-specific behavior.
Keep generated and local-only artifacts outside the tracked source tree from the first commit.

2.subject: feat(runtime): enforce offline Kaggle model resolution
body: Add offline model-resolution helpers for Kaggle-mounted model assets and local source discovery.
Cover resolver behavior and offline-mode enforcement with dedicated unit tests.
Prevent runtime setup from silently depending on network access when the model must resolve locally.

3.subject: feat(runtime): validate dual-T4 model dispatch
body: Add GPU discovery and dispatch compatibility logic for the dual-T4 Kaggle environment.
Cover device selection and dispatch behavior with focused GPU and compatibility tests.
Keep accelerator validation explicit before higher-level model loading is introduced.

4.subject: feat(embedding): add multimodal embedding primitives
body: Add the initial multimodal embedding primitives used by text and image inference paths.
Enforce the right-padding tokenizer contract that EOS pooling depends on and reject left-padding processors before batched inference.
Cover embedding behavior with unit tests alongside the implementation.

5.subject: feat(runtime): load WeMM across both T4 GPUs
body: Add the runtime loader contract that places WeMM across both available T4 devices.
Validate model-loading and runtime expectations with dedicated contract tests.
Make dual-GPU loading behavior explicit before acceptance and evidence collection layers are added.

6.subject: feat(runtime): capture runtime acceptance evidence
body: Add runtime evidence capture for recording verified execution state and acceptance artifacts.
Cover evidence serialization and contract behavior with dedicated tests.
Keep evidence generation separate from the model-loading implementation it observes.

7.subject: feat(kaggle): add runtime acceptance workflow
body: Add Kaggle preflight and acceptance entry points together with their runtime requirements.
Introduce the shared runtime environment helper sourced by launch and setup scripts as their first consumer is added.
Keep the acceptance workflow reproducible through versioned shell and Python entry points.

8.subject: test(runtime): enforce dual-GPU runtime contracts
body: Harden Kaggle setup with explicit setup guards and shell-level runtime contracts.
Add regression coverage for setup validation and shell behavior in the dual-GPU environment.
Fail early when runtime prerequisites do not satisfy the expected deployment contract.

9.subject: feat(benchmark): define statistics and batch progression
body: Define benchmark statistics, batch progression, and the reusable benchmark execution model.
Add tests for statistical summaries and progression across benchmark batches.
Separate benchmark mechanics from later CLI and provenance-recording concerns.

10.subject: test(runtime): enforce repeatable batched inference contracts
body: Add regression coverage for repeatable batched inference behavior, including the right-padding EOS contract.
Reject left-padding tokenizers before batched encoding and keep FAIL-state padding evidence at the Kaggle boundary.
Protect deterministic runtime behavior needed by later performance evidence collection.

11.subject: feat(benchmark): add evidence CLI and provenance recording
body: Add the benchmark CLI, runner contracts, and provenance recording for generated evidence.
Cover CLI behavior, runner execution, and provenance fields with dedicated tests.
Make benchmark evidence attributable to the runtime configuration that produced it.

12.subject: feat(kaggle): add benchmark runtime bootstrap
body: Add the Kaggle benchmark runtime bootstrap script on top of the shared runtime environment.
Keep benchmark launch consistent with the preflight and acceptance entry points.
Cover the shell environment contract used to launch reproducible benchmark runs.

13.subject: build(api): add REST service dependencies
body: Add the dependency set required by the REST API service.
Keep API-specific packages separated from the core Kaggle runtime requirements.
Prepare the repository for service-layer commits without changing inference behavior.

14.subject: feat(api): add authentication configuration and validation
body: Add API authentication, configuration, and request-validation components.
Cover authentication, configuration parsing, and validation behavior with focused tests.
Keep service security and configuration checks explicit at the API boundary.

15.subject: feat(api): add bounded inference scheduler
body: Add a bounded inference scheduler and the state and logging support it requires.
Track model loading under the scheduler lifecycle so shutdown cannot race startup back into READY, and keep shutdown idempotent.
Cover fail-closed submit behavior and controlled request execution with dedicated tests.

16.subject: feat(api): expose multimodal embedding endpoints
body: Expose multimodal embedding operations through the API application and request schemas.
Add application-level tests for the public embedding endpoints.
Connect validated API requests to the bounded inference service without changing embedding semantics.

17.subject: feat(kaggle): add localhost API launcher
body: Add Kaggle scripts for installing and launching the API on localhost.
Provide the service entry point and verify API dependency expectations.
Keep the deployment surface local-first for notebook and tunnel-based demonstrations.

18.subject: test(api): add API acceptance contracts
body: Add a standalone API acceptance driver for service-level request contracts.
Consolidate end-to-end API acceptance checks outside the unit-test implementation.
Provide a repeatable verification entry point for the completed API surface.

19.subject: feat(search): define bilingual Wikidata contracts
body: Define the bilingual Wikidata record and dataset contracts used by the retrieval subsystem.
Establish deterministic English/Vietnamese field handling before storage and retrieval layers are added.
Keep search-domain contracts explicit and independently testable from the runtime and API layers.

20.subject: feat(search): add Qdrant storage and embedding client
body: Add the Qdrant storage adapter and embedding-client boundary required by the search subsystem.
Route canonical, configurable Qdrant collection names end to end and enforce the en/vi named-vector Cosine schema.
Probe the embedding API readiness contract and fail closed unless the runtime reports READY.
Provide focused tests for storage and embedding integration behavior.

21.subject: feat(search): add retrieval service and schemas
body: Add retrieval schemas and the service layer that coordinates embedding requests with Qdrant search.
Keep request/response validation separate from vector-store details and route Qdrant access through public store boundaries.
Root /readyz authority in the actual embedding runtime readiness and cover the service contract with dedicated tests.

22.subject: feat(search): add deterministic Wikidata discovery
body: Add deterministic discovery logic for locating and validating the bilingual Wikidata source dataset.
Make dataset selection explicit so ingestion does not depend on ambiguous filesystem ordering.
Fail closed when the expected source contract cannot be established.

23.subject: feat(search): add deterministic Wikidata ingest
body: Add deterministic Wikidata ingestion with stable point construction for the Qdrant collections.
Preserve repeatable bilingual record handling across reruns of the ingestion workflow.
Keep ingestion validation separate from later qualification and benchmark stages.

24.subject: feat(kaggle): add Qdrant and search launchers
body: Add Kaggle setup and launch scripts for the local Qdrant-backed search service.
Keep the search stack notebook-friendly and bound to the project runtime conventions.
Provide explicit entry points for preparing and starting the retrieval service.

25.subject: feat(search): add qualification workflow
body: Add search qualification checks for the bilingual retrieval path and supporting runtime contracts.
Record the original strict verdict, the approved threshold evaluation, and whether the documented acceptance-policy deviation is actually applied.
Fail closed when required search invariants are not satisfied.

26.subject: feat(search): add repeatable search benchmark
body: Add the repeatable search benchmark used to measure and record bilingual retrieval behavior.
Honor CLI collection overrides end to end and emit the benchmark name in the output schema.
Provide a stable evidence path for later release qualification together with focused benchmark tests.

27.subject: feat(search): add snapshot restore and fail-closed recovery
body: Add verified Qdrant snapshot restore and fail-closed recovery behavior for reusable search data.
Avoid silently continuing from incomplete or dirty local state when snapshot recovery is required.
Cover recovery contracts with dedicated acceptance and unit tests.

28.subject: refactor(runtime): introduce provider-neutral runtime
body: Introduce the provider-neutral wemm_runtime package boundary.
Separate reusable runtime ownership from Kaggle-specific orchestration.
Prepare a stable namespace for the portable runtime components added in subsequent commits.

29.subject: refactor(runtime): add portable runtime primitives
body: Add portable configuration, embedding, GPU, Qdrant, and service primitives.
Enforce the right-padding contract and emit deterministic tokenizer padding evidence at model load.
Preserve existing inference contracts while reducing dependence on Kaggle-specific code paths.

30.subject: refactor(runtime): isolate reusable model worker
body: Isolate model loading and worker execution into reusable runtime components.
Bound subprocess startup, request, and shutdown waits with terminate/kill fallback and drain merged logs through a reader thread.
Verify the JSON-line worker protocol over real subprocess pipes, including timeout, EOF, and reader cleanup.
Keep process ownership and model lifecycle separate from notebook and API presentation layers.

31.subject: refactor(runtime): freeze reusable showcase contracts
body: Add the reusable showcase contract used by portable runtime consumers.
Centralize showcase-facing behavior in the provider-neutral runtime package.
Keep presentation contracts stable before the Kaggle public-demo helpers are layered on top.

32.subject: feat(kaggle): add reusable demo IO helpers
body: Add reusable Kaggle demo configuration and IO helpers.
Separate input, output, and configuration handling from the public-demo orchestrator.
Provide a small shared foundation for notebook-driven demonstration steps.

33.subject: feat(kaggle): preserve verified Qdrant and showcase behavior
body: Preserve the verified Qdrant bootstrap and showcase behavior used by the public demo.
Version the Qdrant retrieval helper and showcase implementation together.
Keep the demonstrated retrieval and presentation behavior aligned with the previously verified Kaggle run.

34.subject: feat(kaggle): add reusable public-demo orchestration
body: Add reusable public-demo orchestration for the Kaggle production notebook.
Centralize demo sequencing and state transitions in a versioned Python module.
Keep notebook cells thin by delegating execution logic to repository code.

35.subject: test(runtime): validate portable runtime contracts
body: Add portable-runtime regression coverage for the provider-neutral runtime boundary.
Defer portable-runtime padding-evidence assertions to this phase where the mirror implementation exists.
Close the runtime and science implementation boundary before publication-only history begins.

36.subject: feat(kaggle): add clean public production demo notebook
body: Add the clean public Kaggle production-demo notebook on top of the verified runtime and retrieval stack.
Ship the modular notebook helpers and demo dependency contract alongside the notebook they support.
Keep public notebook metadata limited to stable reproducibility information and guard that contract with a regression test.
Prepare the project for publication without changing the verified runtime or search behavior.

37.subject: feat(project): publish public demo and documentation suite
body: Publish the complete public demo and documentation suite built on the verified runtime boundary.
Add the publication qualification baseline that the bilingual guide and release records build upon.
Align contributor and development commands with the search dependencies and Markdown-link validation used by CI from the first publication commit.

38.subject: docs(readme): publish bilingual project guide
body: Publish the English and Vietnamese landing guides as one paired documentation change.
Keep the two public README entry points synchronized for installation, runtime, and review guidance.
Preserve bilingual pairing while keeping installation and runtime guidance synchronized.

39.subject: fix(notebook): refine bilingual result table layout
body: Apply the direction-column presentation correction together with its matching regression guard.
Update the text showcase together with its modular-notebook regression guard.
Preserve retrieval semantics while improving the bilingual result-table presentation.

40.subject: fix(notebook): finalize visual evidence presentation
body: Apply the final visual presentation refinement together with its matching regression test.
Update the visual showcase together with its modular-notebook regression guard.
Preserve the 1400px two-column grid and compact visual robustness output without changing retrieval semantics.

41.subject: ci: enforce publication qualification policy
body: Harden the publication CI by moving the publication-policy gate to the final evidence step and pinning the pytest cache mode.
Add the publication-history manifest and validator as the single source of the 42-commit canonical lineage, runtime pin, restored paths, and release qualification evidence.
Enforce documentation, tests, compile, shell, whitespace, runtime-pin reachability, and qualification-statement consistency as the closing authority gate.

42.subject: release: publish v1.0.0
body: Mark the verified 42-commit canonical release history as the first public stable release baseline.

Align the bilingual README, release record, and reproducibility documentation to the v1.0.0 release qualification baseline (470 passed, 3 skipped, 234 Markdown link targets) while treating warning totals as environment-observed evidence rather than a source invariant.
Preserve the verified runtime, retrieval, notebook, documentation, and publication-policy boundaries as the tagged v1.0.0 release.

ci_required_commands: python -m pip install pytest packaging pillow -r requirements-api.txt -r requirements-demo.txt -r requirements-search.txt
